Dave Ross|VIRGINIA TECH OVER 6.5 WINS (-.summary: Ross calls this his one-shot, silver-bullet play and says he is firing on every Virginia Tech future, taking Over 6.5 at -140 and the alternate Over 7.5 at +120. The case is James Franklin in year one: he was in the CFP semifinals two seasons ago before leaving Happy Valley for Blacksburg, and Ross reads that as one programme's discard becoming another's prize. He rates the retention of Brent Pry as defensive coordinator the hidden gem of the hire, calls Virginia Tech one of the biggest winners in the portal, and says he would not be surprised to see them in Charlotte playing for an ACC title.
Dave Ross|VIRGINIA TECH OVER 6.5 WINS (-.depends_on: coaching (Franklin's arrival, Pry retained as DC); portal recruiting

Matt Youmans|FRESNO STATE OVER 6.5 WINS.summary: Youmans builds the case on Matt Entz, who won two FCS national titles at North Dakota State on a 60-11 record and then turned a losing Fresno State team into a 9-4 finish in his first year. He judges that team to have been held back by mediocre quarterback play and notes Entz answered it with Maryland transfer Khristian Martin, a dual-threat. Four of the top five pass catchers return, Josiah Freeman among them, and three of the Pac-12's better offensive linemen block for experienced backs Bryson Donelson and Rayshon Luke. He flags the Oct. 10 home game with Boise State as possibly the most important matchup of Pac-12 play, recalling that Entz's Fresno side won 30-7 at Boise as a 17-point underdog. After a September trip to USC he sees a realistic run of three straight wins over Sacramento State, San Jose State and Rice, and notes Circa posted 6.5 with the league's 12th flex game included.
Matt Youmans|FRESNO STATE OVER 6.5 WINS.depends_on: coaching (Entz year two); quarterback (Khristian Martin); returning receivers and offensive line; schedule

Matt Youmans|MICHIGAN UNDER 8.5 WINS (-1.summary: Youmans argues the Big Ten is loaded again — he names Ohio State, Oregon and Indiana — while Michigan has been losing ground. He traces the fallout from the Harbaugh era to the firing of Sherrone Moore, whose staff he calls clumsy and faults for failing to develop freshman quarterback Bryce Underwood. His summary is that the talent level is down while the schedule's difficulty is up: road trips to Ohio State and Oregon, home games against Indiana, Iowa, Penn State and Oklahoma. He rates the hiring of Kyle Whittingham a substantial positive but says almost everything would have to go right for nine wins, and reads 7-5 as the likelier outcome.
Matt Youmans|MICHIGAN UNDER 8.5 WINS (-1.depends_on: coaching (Moore fired, Whittingham hired); quarterback development; schedule; conference strength

Dave Tuley|TEXAS TO WIN SEC (+295) & NAT.summary: Tuley opens by stating his own method rather than a projection: longtime readers of his columns know he would rather be a year early on a team peaking than a year late, and he is not deterred by a bet coming up short. He bet Texas to win the playoff last season and lost it when Arch Manning did not reach his potential as quickly as hoped; he read the Longhorns' disappointing year as showing signs of competence and is betting that he was simply early, drawing an explicit parallel to backing the Detroit Lions again after losing with them. He notes Texas is the second betting choice in the SEC behind Georgia.
Dave Tuley|TEXAS TO WIN SEC (+295) & NAT.depends_on: quarterback (Arch Manning's development); the contributor's stated willingness to be early

Dave Tuley|INDIANA TO WIN BIG TEN (+245).summary: Tuley notes he was not a believer in Indiana for most of last season but took the Hoosiers at +330 to win the playoff in the VSiN Bowl Betting Guide and rode them to the title. He acknowledges the loss of Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza as the NFL's No. 1 overall pick, but credits Curt Cignetti with one of the biggest turnarounds in the sport's history and says he is confident Indiana will be in the running again. He reads the Big Ten as a three-horse race between Indiana, Ohio State and Oregon, which makes +245 a fair price, and adds he might also take a shot at the Hoosiers repeating as national champion.
Dave Tuley|INDIANA TO WIN BIG TEN (+245).depends_on: coaching (Cignetti); replacing a departed Heisman-winning quarterback; the contributor's read that the league is a three-way race

Dave Tuley|TOLEDO TO WIN MAC (+365).summary: Tuley declares his interest up front — a Northern Illinois alumnus and longtime MAC follower, with mixed feelings about the Huskies leaving for the Mountain West. He reads the MAC as another three-horse race between Toledo, Western Michigan and Miami (OH). The Toledo case is new head coach Mike Jacobs, who he says has won everywhere he has been including back-to-back SoCon titles at Mercer, plus a programme he describes as used to rebuilding after losing coaches and competing every year regardless. He names running back CJ Miller and receiver Adjatay Dabbs among the arrivals from Mercer.
Dave Tuley|TOLEDO TO WIN MAC (+365).depends_on: coaching (Jacobs's arrival and his record); incoming transfers; the contributor's read that the league is a three-way race

Aaron Moore|TEXAS TO WIN NATIONAL CHAMPI.summary: Moore signs up for what he calls the Arch Manning redemption tour, arguing the quarterback who started last season was far from able to lead a national title team while the version at the end of it was much closer. Beyond added experience for Manning and lead receiver Ryan Wingo, he notes Texas added a downfield threat in Auburn transfer Cam Coleman, and expects Will Muschamp on the sideline to help the defense. He frames 7-1 as a buy-low after three straight national championships for the Big Ten, on what he expects to be one of the two best teams in the SEC.
Aaron Moore|TEXAS TO WIN NATIONAL CHAMPI.depends_on: quarterback (Manning's late-season form); portal addition at receiver; coaching (Muschamp on defense)

Aaron Moore|CLEMSON UNDER 5.5 CONFERENCE.summary: Moore's case is the schedule rather than the roster. He allows that Clemson is warming to the portal, but argues the ACC's draw makes six conference wins hard: a mid-September flight to Berkeley sandwiched between home games with North Carolina and Miami, and three of the last four on the road.

Aaron Moore|SMU TO REACH ACC CHAMPIONSHI.summary: Moore makes the bet conditional and says so: if veteran quarterback Kevin Jennings can win at least one of SMU's opening two conference games, at Florida State and at Louisville, he sees the Mustangs well set for the rest of ACC play, with plenty of October and November wins available. He notes the finale at Stanford follows a trip to South Bend but says it is hard to envision Stanford blocking a championship-game appearance.
Aaron Moore|SMU TO REACH ACC CHAMPIONSHI.depends_on: quarterback (Kevin Jennings); schedule (the opening two conference games as the hinge)

Steve Makinen|TEXAS TO MAKE COLLEGE FOOT.summary: Makinen's case is talent accumulation: over two springs the Texas staff signed the No. 1 and No. 3 ranked recruit and transfer classes per 247Sports, which to him makes this probably the most talented locker room in the country. He allows the talent still has to be developed but credits Steve Sarkisian with having done exactly that, taking Texas to the playoff title game two years ago. He reads last season's expectations as unrealistic, with the pressure on the programme and on Arch Manning visible every week, and points out the Longhorns still won 10 games despite a 5-7-1 ATS record.
Steve Makinen|TEXAS TO MAKE COLLEGE FOOT.depends_on: recruiting and portal classes; coaching (Sarkisian); quarterback (Manning)

Steve Makinen|BOISE STATE TO MAKE COLLEG.summary: Makinen expects one Group of Five team in the playoff this year rather than the two that got in last season, and names Boise State as the likeliest candidate as they move to the new Pac-12. Running his updated power ratings against the 2026 schedule produced a +1.7 win difference he calls one of the biggest he has ever had. He argues the oddsmakers are crediting the new conference's strength too generously when Boise State is its clear favourite, notes Maddux Madsen returns at quarterback as a senior and Spencer Danielson is in his fourth year, and identifies the opener at Oregon as the only likely loss on the slate.
Steve Makinen|BOISE STATE TO MAKE COLLEG.depends_on: power rating versus schedule; quarterback (Madsen); coaching (Danielson, year four); conference realignment

Steve Makinen|UNLV TO MAKE MOUNTAIN WEST.summary: Makinen says he has worked through UNLV's 2026 schedule — now without Boise State, who left for the Pac-12 — and is struggling to find a single game where the Rebels would not be favoured or at least highly competitive. Given New Mexico's rise last year, he reads UNLV's sustained Mountain West consistency as making them the league favourite. He credits Dan Mullen with recruiting classes that carry on a 30-12 run over three years and with attracting numerous Power Four transfers, Auburn quarterback Jackson Arnold among them.
Steve Makinen|UNLV TO MAKE MOUNTAIN WEST.depends_on: schedule (Boise State's departure); coaching (Mullen); portal recruiting; quarterback (Jackson Arnold)

Tyler Shoemaker|ARKANSAS UNDER 4.5 WINS.summary: Shoemaker argues from his TSI model's game-by-game win probabilities rather than from narrative. TSI projects 4.3 wins. Combing the schedule he finds only two games above a 60% win probability and ten below 40%, with nothing in between that he would call a coin flip. His framing of the risk is arithmetic: for the Under to lose, Arkansas must win both games it is supposed to win and then substantially overachieve in three more.
Tyler Shoemaker|ARKANSAS UNDER 4.5 WINS.depends_on: model projection and game-by-game win probabilities; schedule

Tyler Shoemaker|SOUTHERN MISS UNDER 3.5.summary: Shoemaker thinks some models — he names FPI — are crediting Southern Miss too heavily for last season, when head coach Charles Huff has since left for Memphis and the programme is undergoing turnover for a second straight year. He expects a major step back, with TSI projecting 3.3 wins, one game above a 60% win probability, ten below 40% and a single coin flip. For the Under to lose he says they must win the one they should, take the coin flip, and add two more as sizable underdogs.
Tyler Shoemaker|SOUTHERN MISS UNDER 3.5.depends_on: coaching (Huff's departure); consecutive roster turnover; model projection

Paul Stone|TEXAS TECH TO WIN BIG 12 CHAM.summary: Stone treats the Brendan Sorsby saga as mostly resolved and turns to Texas Tech defending its Big 12 title. He calls quarterback the clear question but reports every indication that Will Hammond will be ready for the Sept. 5 opener against Abilene Christian after tearing an ACL the previous October. He argues Hammond is not a novice, having started the 2024 Liberty Bowl against Arkansas and two games last season relieving an injured Behren Morton, and says that with Hammond healthy Texas Tech projects as a double-digit favourite in all twelve regular-season games.

Paul Stone|BYU +3 VS. UTAH (GAME OF THE.summary: Stone frames this as a coaching-experience edge in a single game: Utah's longtime defensive coordinator Morgan Scalley is a first-time head coach, while BYU's Kalani Sitake — who worked alongside Scalley in Salt Lake City for nearly a decade — enters his eleventh season. He also believes BYU has the better roster, citing sophomore quarterback Bear Bachmeier's surprising true-freshman year and senior back LJ Martin's 1,305 rushing yards in 2025, whom he calls one of the nation's most underappreciated. Against that he sets Utah's questions on both lines, and notes BYU is 23-4 straight up over two seasons. He likes BYU to win outright in Salt Lake City.
